name: CROWNING MOMENTS
clue: Born in 1769, a year after Genoa ceded his island birthplace to France, he crowned himself emperor in Notre-Dame in 1804

name: IT'S ALL GREEK TO HER
clue: Egypt's last active pharaoh, she was a native Greek speaker descended from one of Alexander the Great's generals

name: DYING DECLARATIONS
clue: Rivals turned pen pals, these 2 Founding Fathers died hours apart on July 4, 1826, their Declaration's 50th anniversary

name: GREAT EXPECTATIONS
clue: Born a minor German princess named Sophie, she seized the Russian throne from her own husband in a 1762 coup

name: FULL CIRCLE
clue: Killed in a Philippine island battle in 1521, he didn't live to complete the first circumnavigation his expedition finished

name: BY ANY OTHER NAME
clue: Constantine renamed Byzantium for himself in 330 A.D.; since 1930 the city bridging the Bosporus has officially used this name

name: LOW POINTS
clue: Bathers bob like corks in this lake between Israel & Jordan, whose shore, about 1,400 feet below sea level, is Earth's lowest land

name: TREE'S COMPANY
clue: The Americas' only Portuguese-speaking nation took its name from a tree whose heartwood yields a flame-red dye

name: ELEMENT OF SURPRISE
clue: Spotted in the Sun's spectrum during an 1868 eclipse and named for a Greek god, it wasn't found on Earth until 1895

name: MOLD RUSH
clue: Back from vacation in 1928, Alexander Fleming found a stray mold wiping out staph colonies, the source of this drug

name: ONCE IN A LIFETIME
clue: Mark Twain was born 2 weeks after its 1835 appearance and died, as he had predicted, the day after its 1910 return

name: STRANGER THAN FICTION
clue: Convinced its first pelt was stitched together as a hoax, naturalists in 1799 hunted in vain for seams on this odd mammal

name: FOR THE RECORD
clue: 'Mary had a little lamb' were the first words this Menlo Park inventor recited into his new phonograph in 1877

name: A DARK & STORMY NIGHT
clue: Subtitled 'The Modern Prometheus,' this novel sprang from an 1816 ghost-story contest at Lord Byron's villa on Lake Geneva

name: SCHOOL TIES
clue: Shakespeare enrolled this brooding prince at Wittenberg, the university town where Martin Luther posted his 95 theses

name: ONE-BOOK WONDER
clue: Her Pulitzer-winning 1960 story of Scout, Jem & Atticus stood as her only published novel for the next 55 years

name: PLAY IT AGAIN
clue: An unproduced play called 'Everybody Comes to Rick's' became this film, the Best Picture Oscar winner for 1943

name: DRAWN TO GREATNESS
clue: Skeptics dubbed it 'Disney's Folly'; this 1937 feature earned Walt an honorary Oscar — one statuette plus 7 miniatures

name: FACE THE MUSIC
clue: At the 1824 premiere of his Ninth Symphony, a soloist turned this composer around so he could see the ovation he couldn't hear

name: HIGH FIVES
clue: On April 4, 1964, this band pulled off a Billboard first, holding all 5 of the Hot 100's top 5 positions at once

name: DRINK TO THAT
clue: Its melody began as 'To Anacreon in Heaven,' a London club's drinking tune; Congress made it official in 1931

name: FRAME JOB
clue: A former Louvre handyman walked off with this portrait in 1911; it resurfaced in Florence more than 2 years later

name: CEILING THE DEAL
clue: Protesting that painting was not his art, this sculptor of 'David' spent 4 years frescoing a ceiling for Pope Julius II

name: UNIFORM DECISION
clue: In 1997, 50 years after he broke in with Brooklyn, this pioneer's No. 42 was retired across every big-league clubhouse

name: GOING THE DISTANCE
clue: This event's exact 26-mile-385-yard length traces to the 1908 London Games' course, Windsor Castle to the royal box

name: BOXED IN
clue: In Hesiod, the gods crafted her as the first mortal woman; she unsealed a jar, loosing every ill but leaving hope inside

name: GODS ON THE CALENDAR
clue: English names this weekday for the Norse thunder god; the French 'jeudi' honors Jupiter, Rome's own thunderer

name: FIT FOR A QUEEN
clue: Tradition credits an 1889 royal visit to Naples for this pizza, whose 3 toppings match the colors of Italy's flag

name: ROYAL READING
clue: Commissioned at the 1604 Hampton Court Conference, this English translation of scripture appeared 7 years later

name: SAVED BY THE SIGNAL
clue: Granted just a 20-year permit for the 1889 World's Fair, it won a reprieve largely for its value as a radio antenna
